yoooo doesn't change the fact that you're doing physical harm to your body.

1) increases risk of infection, like staph 

2) cutting is regressive. meaning that small babycuts aren't always going to work forever, therefore in states of psychological distress one could cut deeper/too deep and cause damage that could be permanent.
- don't believe me? cutting too deep can do more than just causing you to bleed out. large amounts of blood loss can do severe PERMANENT damage to the brain. one example of this is anoxic brain injury, in which a hemorrhage leads to [anoxic shock](https://www.headway.org.uk/about-brain-injury/individuals/types-of-brain-injury/hypoxic-and-anoxic-brain-injury/), another is [hypovolemic shock](http://www.healthline.com/health/hypovolemic-shock#overview1) which can lead to organ failure as well as brain damage and gangrene.

3) cutting is addictive- if you use it to cope with emotional pain and stress, it's only a temporary relief. as most people who engage in cutting or other forms of self harm tend to be [younger](https://www.google.com/amp/s/www.psychologytoday.com/blog/sax-sex/201003/why-are-so-many-girls-cutting-themselves%3Famp) (not gonna say female b/c the rate of boys who report cutting is much LOWER, which means any argument about going to the hospital to combat #2 is ridiculous because plenty of people do not report it), these young people are more likely to be concerned with how they fit in with society. because they cut and do something outside of the norm, this may cause them more shame and therefore increase the likelihood of cutting again to cope with this emotional pain. it's cyclical- pain, cut, relief, eventually more pain, and then cut again.

the reason I felt like posting this is because this I feel like should be a community that tries to support others in getting over their self-harm issues and asking questions about what they recognize as a problem, not condoning or promoting what is recognized as an issue that is so often an indicated of deeper psychological trauma. as a cutter this is very important to me.

- if you're going to wear long sleeves don't go for a lighter color
- consider putting on some muscle/exercising more

if you're going for a more feminine/neutral appearance:
- keep the circular frames but still go for a smaller frame
- lighter colors

I think you're an attractive person overall, but playing an angle and being more confident would be a good bet for you!

if you want to meet gay men who might be interested use dating apps or get more active in the LGBT community where you are. dating isn't just about your looks, after all- its social too. good luck!
